title: Participles 1: Active Present (-щий)
description: The Russian participle (причастие) is a verb-derived adjective. Today: the active present participle (the noun performs the action right now). Formation rule: 3rd-person plural minus ending plus -щ plus adjective endings.
descriptionRussian: Русское причастие — это отглагольное прилагательное. Сегодня: действительное причастие настоящего времени (определяемое слово само совершает действие в настоящий момент). Правило: от формы третьего лица множественного числа отсекаем личное окончание и присоединяем -щ + окончания прилагательного.
intro: A participle is a verb dressed as an adjective. It carries an action but behaves like a describing word, agreeing with its noun in gender, number and case. Russian has four of them, sorted by two questions: is the noun doing the action or receiving it, and is that happening now or already done. This book takes one at a time, starting with the noun doing something right now.
rules: An active present participle is a verb-derived adjective expressing an action that the noun is performing right now: a reading person → читающий человек.

Formation: from the third-person plural present (читают, говорят, идут), drop the personal ending and add the participle suffix + the adjective endings (-ий / -ая / -ее / -ие). The suffix mirrors the 3pl ending you just dropped: -ут → -ущ- (идущий), -ют → -ющ- (читающий), -ат → -ащ- (дышащий, after ж ш щ ч ц), -ят → -ящ- (говорящий, любящий).
Only imperfective verbs form active present participles. Perfective verbs have no present tense to build from; their active participle is the past form (lesson 2).
Active present participles agree with their noun in gender, number, and case, like any adjective: о читающем человеке, к читающей женщине, читающих детей.
examples: держат → держащий ребёнка отец (a father holding the child)
Сидящий в углу мужчина — мой брат. (The man sitting in the corner is my brother.)

tables.title: Adjective endings for active present participles

items.prompt: What is the active present participle of читать?
items.promptEnglish: Form the active present participle of читать.
items.hint: Find the third-person plural present (читают). Drop the ending and add the suffix plus the masculine singular adjective ending.
items.explanation: Читать is imperfective, so it has an active present participle. From читают, drop -ют to get чита-, add -ющ- + -ий → читающий. Читая is the imperfective gerund (a different form); прочитавший is the active past participle of perfective прочитать (lesson 2); читаемый is the passive present participle (lesson 3).

items.prompt: Form the active present participle of говорить.
items.hint: From говорят, drop -ят. Which suffix follows a 2nd-conjugation stem?
items.explanation: Говорят → говор- + -ящ- + -ий = говорящий (speaking, masc sg). The suffix is -ящ- because the 3pl ending is -ят, not -ют. Говоря is the gerund; сказавший is the active past participle of perfective сказать; говоривший is the active past participle of говорить (lesson 2).

items.prompt: Pick the feminine singular form of the active present participle of читать.
items.promptEnglish: Which is the feminine singular form?
items.hint: Which adjective ending is feminine singular?
items.explanation: Feminine singular adjective ending is -ая, so the feminine form is читающая (e.g., читающая женщина). Читающий is masculine singular; читающее is neuter singular; читающих is the genitive or prepositional plural.

items.prompt: Which of these is the active present participle of идти?
items.promptEnglish: Pick the active present participle of идти (to go on foot).
items.hint: Find the form built from the 3pl present (идут) + -ущ- + adjective ending.
items.explanation: Идут → ид- + -ущ- + -ий = идущий (the person who is walking). Шёл is the past tense; идти is the infinitive; шедший is the active PAST participle of идти (lesson 2).

items.prompt: Сидящий в углу мужчина — мой брат. What does сидящий mean?
items.promptEnglish: Translate сидящий in the sentence above.
items.hint: Сидящий is the active present participle of сидеть.
items.explanation: Сидящий is the active present participle of сидеть. It modifies мужчина: the man who is sitting (right now, at the same time as 'is my brother'). English uses the relative clause 'who is sitting'; Russian compresses it into one participle phrase. 'While sitting' would be the gerund сидя.

items.prompt: Which verb CANNOT form an active present participle?
items.promptEnglish: Pick the verb that has no active present participle.
items.hint: Only one aspect can derive an active present participle.
items.explanation: Прочитать is perfective. Perfective verbs have no present tense (only past and future-completed), so they have no 'present' base to build from. Active present participles come only from imperfective verbs. Прочитать DOES form an active past participle (прочитавший), the topic of lesson 2.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Active present participle, plural form. The children are playing at the same time as their laughing.
hints: The slot needs a plural participle describing children performing the activity right now. Which form fits?
explanations: Играющие is the active present participle of играть, plural (matching дети). The children are playing at the same time as their laughing. Играть is the infinitive; играли is the finite past tense; игравшие is the active past participle (lesson 2), meaning 'who had been playing earlier.'

errorCorrection.sentence: Пишащий письмо студент сидел у окна.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The student writing a letter was sitting by the window.
errorCorrection.explanation: Писать is 1st-conjugation (пишут, -ут), so the active present suffix is -ущ-: пишущий. The suffix mirrors the 3pl ending you drop, and -ут gives -ущ-, never -ащ-. Писавший is the past participle and пишемый a passive form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The sleeping child didn't hear the doorbell.
errorCorrection.explanation: Спать is 2nd-conjugation (спят, -ят), so the active present suffix is -ящ-: спящий. The suffix copies the 3pl ending you drop, and -ят gives -ящ-, not the 1st-conjugation -ющ-. Спавший is the past participle; спимый is not a usable form.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The man running through the park was smiling.
errorCorrection.explanation: Бежать takes -ут in the 3pl (бегут), so the active present suffix is -ущ-: бегущий. The -ут ending yields -ущ-, never -ящ-. Бегящий wrongly guesses -ящ- (as in говорящий). Бегавший and бежавший are past participles.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I know students who study Russian.
minimalPairs.explanation: The slot needs a participle agreeing with студентов (animate masculine plural in the accusative, which matches the genitive plural form). Изучающих is that form. Изучают is the finite 3rd-person plural verb, which would need который (которые изучают), not a participle.

reviewVocab.definition: participle (a verb-derived adjective; carries an action at its core but functions like an adjective, agreeing with the noun in gender, number, and case)
reviewVocab.example: Читающий, читавший, читаемый, прочитанный — все это причастия от глаголов 'читать' и 'прочитать'.

reviewVocab.definition: active participle (the noun the participle modifies is the one performing the action; passive participles flip the relation)
reviewVocab.example: Читающий человек — человек, который читает (он сам совершает действие).

reviewVocab.definition: present tense (the time relation expressed by an active present participle: the action holds at the same time as the main verb)
reviewVocab.example: Сидящий мужчина сидит сейчас — в момент главного глагола.

reviewVocab.definition: modifier / attribute (the syntactic role the participle plays in the noun phrase: a word that describes the noun)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'читающий человек' слово 'читающий' — определение к существительному 'человек'.
